title: Marked Type II estimates for prime predecessors
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's one-sided marked Type II estimate for prime predecessors: bilinear sums of the prime indicator minus its rough-number average against arbitrary rough coefficients, at the predecessors mn - 1 and weighted by marks from fixed bands of primes, are smaller than every power of log x. A coefficient criterion; a zero-free strip at large height and long prime polynomials; Cauchy's inequality and a determinant equation; physical states, root residues and independent lines; lifespans, a memory of pending primes and contraction on clean and dirty edges; birth distinctness; the major arcs by characters, Mellin separation and sparse frequencies.
prerequisites: Counting primes by elementary means: Chebyshev and Mertens (course NT-ZETA, lesson NT-ZETA-02, Theorems 3.1 and 4.2)
Mean values of Dirichlet polynomials (NT-ZETA-16, Theorem 2.1)
Exponential sums: Kusmin–Landau, the second-derivative test and van der Corput's inequality (NT-ZETA-07, Theorems 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1)
Jensen's formula (NT-ZETA-05, Theorem 1.1 and inequality (4)); Landau's lemma (NT-ZETA-13, Theorem 1.1); the zeta function near s = 1 and the positivity identity (NT-ZETA-08, (1.1) and Lemma 3.1)
Dirichlet series and Euler products (NT-ZETA-01, Lemma A.2: Cauchy's theorem), used in lesson 6
Schwartz functions and Fourier inversion (course AN-01, prerequisite page prerequisites/U011-free-foundations/schwartz-fourier-foundations-U017, Section F4), used in lessons 6 and 17

Lebesgue integration and smoothing, selected programme proofs (course AN-01, prerequisite page prerequisites/U011-free-foundations/banach-foundation-bridges, Sections 15.1 and 15.2: Tonelli's theorem, Cauchy's and Hölder's inequalities for integrals), used in lesson 17
Measure and Hilbert space tools for Haar integration (course harmonic-analysis-on-locally-compact-groups, Theorem 3.1: Hölder's inequality), used in lessons 4 and 9
